title: Drain-safe SDDC Manager credential rotation
prompt:
Make credential rotation in the vcfcred package drain-safe and fix how it encodes request bodies. vcfcred is a standard-library-only Python package under src/ that rotates an SDDC Manager service-account password against the VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 SDDC Manager REST API. It already reaches every operation it needs (createToken, getCredentials, updateOrRotatePasswords, getCredentialsTask, getCredential) and it already polls the credentials task to a terminal status instead of trusting the 202 acknowledgement. Two things are wrong.

CredentialBroker.rotate shuts the lease gate and then submits the rotation straight away, so requests that had already borrowed the outgoing password are still in flight when SDDC Manager applies the change and they come back 401. Rotation must resolve the credential first, then shut the gate, then wait for the leases that are already outstanding to be released, and only then submit updateOrRotatePasswords. A caller blocked on the shut gate holds no lease and must not be waited for. A caller that waits through a rotation must come out of CredentialBroker.lease holding the replacement password, not the one that was current when it arrived. Several callers must be able to hold leases at the same time, so do not serialize everything behind one exclusive lock. The gate has to reopen whether the task ends SUCCESSFUL or FAILED; a FAILED task leaves the existing password in place and must raise RotationFailed.

Second, build_update_spec and build_token_spec pad their JSON with placeholders. An optional property the caller has no value for must be absent from the object rather than sent as an empty string or as null. For a ROTATE the replacement password is chosen by SDDC Manager, so BaseCredential.password is not sent at all, and resourceId, autoRotatePolicy, apiKey and idToken are omitted when unset. Build the spec from the values held on the TargetCredential; do not backfill it from what getCredentials returned.

Keep the existing public API. docs/contract.json is the local REST contract for these operations and docs/official_sources.json records the specification it was derived from. Run python3 -B tests/verify.py. Only src/ is implementation; docs/ and tests/ are protected fixtures and must not be changed.
